tools.name: deploy_site
tools.description: Publish a static website (HTML, CSS, JS, images) to the Press5 launch pad and get its live URL. Works with no account: without a token the site gets a random name, goes live at once, and the reply has a claim_url for the person to keep it (unclaimed sites are deleted after 3 days) and a site_key to

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the sites on this Press5 account, with their URLs and status, plus the account limits.

tools.name: site_info
tools.description: One site with its recent deploys (ids for rollback_site).

tools.name: rollback_site
tools.description: Put an earlier deploy of a site back live. Get deploy ids from site_info.

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Delete a site and all its deploys. It goes offline at once and the name becomes free for anyone. Ask the person first.

tools.name: login_start
tools.description: Start signing in to the Press5 launch pad when you have no token. Press5 emails the person a link to approve this tool (it also creates a free account for a new email). Then call login_check.

tools.name: login_check
tools.description: Check whether the person approved the sign-in from login_start. Call it every few seconds after they say they have pressed Approve. Returns the token once.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "deploy_site" is 682 chars, far longer than this server's median (118). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: deploy_site, list_sites · Private data: deploy_site, login_start, login_check · Public sink: deploy_site, login_start · Destructive: delete_site.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: deploy_site, list_sites · Private data: deploy_site, login_start, login_check · Public sink: deploy_site, login_start · Destructive: delete_site

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
